name: Device lock and passcode state
plain: Reads whether the phone has a screen lock and whether it is locked.
meaning: A phone with no lock is a risk flag; banking apps change flows on it.

ios.api_surface: No direct passcode-set API; probe by saving a Keychain item that needs a passcode

limits.headline: Can tell if your phone has a screen lock and whether it is locked now
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app checks device security
can: Check if the phone is protected by a PIN, pattern, password or biometric
Check if the screen is locked right now (Android)
Use the answer to allow or refuse sensitive features
On iPhone, guess that a passcode exists by trying to save a protected item
cannot: See your PIN, pattern or passcode
On iPhone, ask directly whether a passcode is set; there is no direct way to ask
limits.reach_label: A yes or no about your lock
limits.differs: Android answers directly. iPhone has no direct question, so apps use an indirect test.

story.what_it_is: An app can tell whether your phone has a screen lock and whether it is locked right now.

marketing.name: Device security checks
marketing.pitch: Android shows apps whether the device is protected by a lock screen so sensitive features can be limited.

story.for_you: You do not see this check. You notice only that some apps, like a wallet or work app, refuse to run until you set a screen lock. Some also hide your data the moment the phone locks.
story.for_makers: Apps that hold money or private data want a lock on the phone before they show it. It is cheap to check and lowers the chance that a lost phone becomes a stolen account.

use_cases.example: A bank app will not open on a phone with no passcode, because anyone who picks it up could move money.
A mobile wallet asks you to set a screen lock before it will store a card for tap to pay.
A work email app blocks company mail on any phone that has no screen lock, as set by IT.
A health app holding test results refuses to show them on an unlocked phone, or locks itself after a short time.
A smart lock app only lets you issue a digital key if the phone itself is protected by a code.
A fraud engine marks sessions from phones with no lock as higher risk and asks for extra proof.

story.android_note: Android apps can ask if a lock is set (KeyguardManager) and whether the device is currently locked.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps can learn whether a passcode is set only indirectly, by asking the system to check, and cannot see the lock status itself.
